# Marlow Jorvvane

Marlow Jorvvane is a Satellite Data Scientist currently employed at Nexlet Robotics, a company specializing in automating roof condition scoring to accelerate insurers’ claims processing. Since joining Nexlet Robotics in 2021, Marlow has focused on developing advanced algorithms for assessing roof damage using multispectral satellite imagery, significantly enhancing the accuracy and speed of post-catastrophe evaluations.

Prior to joining Nexlet Robotics, Marlow worked from 2017 to 2021 as a Remote Sensing Analyst at AeroDyne Solutions, where they led the optimization of flood mapping models for inland water bodies using high-resolution drone data. Marlow’s work there involved integrating multispectral and thermal data streams to improve detection of flood extents and water depth estimations, resulting in the project codenamed “BlueCurrent,” which helped local governments reduce flood response times by an estimated 30%.

Marlow’s specialties include designing machine learning pipelines for multispectral data preprocessing, feature extraction, and damage classification tailored to the insurance industry’s needs. Their expertise in combining multispectral bands with topographic and weather data enables robust roof condition scoring models that can differentiate between minor wear and catastrophic damage. A key project at Nexlet Robotics, internally named “SkyGuard,” utilized these techniques to automatically flag high-risk properties within 24 hours after major storms, reducing manual inspection workloads by 45%.

Known for a collaborative and methodical working style, Marlow emphasizes clear communication of complex data science concepts to cross-functional teams. They regularly partner with software engineers, catastrophe modelers, and claims adjusters to ensure algorithm outputs meet operational requirements. Marlow is also proactive in mentoring junior data scientists, fostering a culture of continuous learning within the satellite analytics team.

Marlow holds a Master’s degree in Geospatial Analytics and Remote Sensing from the University of Ellenton and has published multiple white papers on multispectral data fusion techniques. Their blend of field experience and academic research contributes to Nexlet Robotics’ leadership in satellite-based insurance analytics.
